context.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It ensures strict regional data residency, regulatory compliance, and resilience for low-bandwidth rural users.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) and Licensed Clinicians (System Users)
- External Pharmacies (EU & US)
- API Gateway & Edge Service with Envoy Sidecar Proxy
- Core Telehealth Services (User Profiles, Video Sessions, Consent Management)
- AI Symptom Checker Engine
- E-Prescription Integration Service
- Regional Data Tier (Cloud SQL, WORM Cloud Storage)
- GCP Regional Infrastructure (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`)

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians to API Gateway: HTTPS / WebRTC
- API Gateway to Core Telehealth Services: gRPC / REST over internal VPC
- AI Symptom Checker to Regional WORM Storage: Secure audit logging over HTTPS
- E-Prescription Service to External Pharmacies: HL7 FHIR (US) and National Standards (EU) via Mutual TLS / HTTPS

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Primary cloud provider utilizing `europe-west3` and `us-central1` regions for regional isolation
- Kubernetes (GKE): Orchestrates stateless microservices across independent regional clusters
- Envoy Proxy: Sidecar proxy handling WebRTC traffic shaping and adaptive bitrate throttling for low-bandwidth resilience
- Cloud SQL: Region-locked managed databases guaranteeing GDPR and HIPAA data residency compliance
- Cloud Storage (WORM / Bucket Lock): Secures immutable AI symptom-checker decision logs for audit traceability

## Rationale
The federated regional architecture on GCP strictly enforces GDPR and HIPAA data residency constraints by keeping EU health data in `europe-west3` and US data in `us-central1`. Edge termination, Envoy sidecars, and immutable WORM logging ensure high availability for low-bandwidth rural users and rigorous audit traceability for EU MDR compliance.

## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. It ensures strict data residency, compliance, and adaptive performance for low-bandwidth users.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) and Licensed Clinicians
- Platform Administrators / Compliance Officers
- External Pharmacies (EU & US)
- Web Frontend (PWA) built with Next.js/React
- API Gateway using Envoy and Cloud Load Balancing
- Core Backend services using Go/Spring Boot
- AI Symptom Checker using Python/FastAPI
- Integration / Interoperability Service using Node.js/Java
- Media Relaying Service using LiveKit (SFU/MCU)
- Data Storage using Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) and Cloud Storage
- Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) clusters in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`

## Relationships
- Web Frontend to API Gateway via HTTPS/WSS (WebRTC/WebSockets)
- API Gateway to Core Backend via REST/gRPC
- Core Backend to AI Symptom Checker via gRPC
- Core Backend to Integration Service via gRPC
- Integration Service to External Pharmacies via HL7 FHIR (US) and national e-prescription adapters (EU)
- Client apps to Media Relaying Service via WebRTC

## Technology Stack
- Next.js/React: Delivers a lightweight PWA for unstable rural connections
- Envoy / Cloud Load Balancing: Manages secure ingress traffic
- Go/Spring Boot: Powers robust core backend business logic
- Python/FastAPI: Executes AI symptom checker microservices
- LiveKit: Provides adaptive bitrate WebRTC media streaming for low-bandwidth resilience
- PostgreSQL / Cloud SQL: Secures regionalized health records per strict data residency rules
- Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): Orchestrates containerized workloads across GCP regions

## Rationale
Regional GKE container deployment in `europe-west3` and `us-central1` strictly enforces GDPR and HIPAA data residency constraints. Modular integration adapters and adaptive WebRTC streaming ensure cross-border scalability and high availability in low-bandwidth environments.

Web Frontend (PWA).analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and the US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance (GDPR/HIPAA/EU MDR), and high availability for rural areas.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) & Licensed Clinicians
- Web Frontend (PWA) (Next.js / React)
- API Gateway (Envoy & Cloud Load Balancing)
- Media Relaying Service (LiveKit SFU/MCU)
- Core Backend services (Go / Spring Boot)
- AI Symptom Checker (Python / FastAPI)
- Data Storage (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL & Cloud Storage)

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians -> Web Frontend (PWA): Accesses telehealth and video consultations [HTTPS / WSS]
- Web Frontend (PWA) -> API Gateway: Sends API requests and WebSocket traffic [HTTPS / WSS]
- Web Frontend (PWA) -> Media Relaying Service: Streams video and audio for consultations [WebRTC]
- API Gateway -> Core Backend services: Routes internal microservice requests [gRPC / HTTPS]
- Core Backend services -> Data Storage: Persists transactional health records [PostgreSQL Protocol / TLS]

## Technology Stack
- Next.js / React: Delivers a Progressive Web App (PWA) with offline-first capabilities for low-bandwidth rural connections.
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Hosts infrastructure across `europe-west3` and `us-central1` to enforce data residency.
- LiveKit: Manages real-time video and audio streaming with adaptive simulcast.
- IndexedDB & Service Workers: Enables local caching and offline payload queuing.

## Rationale
The architecture enforces strict regional isolation to comply with GDPR and HIPAA mandates. The PWA and adaptive WebRTC streaming ensure reliable care in unstable rural environments.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
[The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients while ensuring strict regional data residency. The API Gateway manages secure ingress traffic, enforces data residency, and handles resilience for unstable connections.]

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) and Licensed Clinicians
- Web Frontend (PWA) built with Next.js / React
- API Gateway container using Google Cloud Load Balancing and Envoy Proxy
- Core Backend services (Go / Spring Boot)
- AI Symptom Checker (Python / FastAPI)
- Edge Load Balancer (Google Cloud Load Balancing)
- Routing & Regional Affinity Engine (Envoy Proxy)
- Security & Policy Filter (Envoy WASM Plugin)
- Resilience & Telemetry Adapter (Envoy Circuit Breaker & Stats Filter)
- Audit & Logging Interceptor (Envoy gRPC Access Log Service - ALS)

## Relationships
- Web Frontend -> Edge Load Balancer [HTTPS / WSS]
- Edge Load Balancer -> Routing & Regional Affinity Engine [gRPC]
- Routing & Regional Affinity Engine -> Core Backend services [gRPC / REST, regionalized per R-05]
- Security & Policy Filter -> Core Backend services [Internal Consent Header Propagation]
- Audit & Logging Interceptor -> Cloud Logging [Asynchronous gRPC ALS streams]

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP) across `europe-west3` and `us-central1` regions for regional data residency enforcement
- Envoy Proxy and Google Cloud Load Balancing for high-performance ingress routing and circuit breaking
- WebAssembly (WASM) for efficient, low-latency JWT validation and consent header injection
- gRPC Access Log Service (ALS) for asynchronous, non-blocking compliance auditing

## Rationale
[This architecture enforces strict regional containment to satisfy GDPR and HIPAA data residency mandates without failing over across regions. Furthermore, it integrates resilient traffic management and asynchronous logging to support rural connectivity needs and regulatory accountability.]

Core Backend services.analysis:
## Overview
A cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients on GCP. It enforces strict regional data residency, regulatory compliance, and resilience for rural areas.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) and Licensed Clinicians
- Web Frontend (PWA) (Next.js / React)
- API Gateway (Envoy and Cloud Load Balancing)
- Core Backend services (Go / Spring Boot) consisting of Consent & Policy Engine, Consultation Orchestrator, Clinical Record Manager, Audit & Compliance Logger, and Session State Cache (Redis / Memorystore)
- AI Symptom Checker (Python / FastAPI)
- Integration / Interoperability Service (Node.js / Java)
- Media Relaying Service (LiveKit SFU/MCU)
- Data Storage (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL and Cloud Storage WORM buckets)

## Relationships
- Web Frontend -> API Gateway: Accesses platform services [HTTPS / WebSocket]
- API Gateway -> Core Backend services: Routes and authorizes requests [gRPC]
- Consent & Policy Engine -> Audit & Compliance Logger: Emits access and consent decisions [gRPC]
- Consultation Orchestrator -> Session State Cache: Buffers ephemeral session states [Redis Protocol]
- Core Backend services -> AI Symptom Checker: Requests AI symptom analysis [gRPC]
- Core Backend services -> Data Storage: Persists records and audit logs [PostgreSQL Protocol / WORM Storage]

## Technology Stack
- GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Isolated multi-region infrastructure enforcing regional data residency.
- Go & Spring Boot: High-concurrency backend services and complex domain logic.
- Redis (Memorystore): Ephemeral session buffering for rural connection drops.
- PostgreSQL (Cloud SQL) & WORM Cloud Storage: Transactional persistence and immutable, encrypted audit logging.
- OpenTelemetry & ArgoCD: Distributed tracing and GitOps regional deployment isolation.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict GDPR and HIPAA compliance by isolating regional data workloads while supporting high-availability video care in rural areas. The modular Go and Spring Boot backend guarantees audit traceability for medical devices and robust resilience against intermittent connectivity.

AI Symptom Checker.analysis:
## Overview
[The AI Symptom Checker container uses a Python/FastAPI microservice architecture deployed on Google Cloud Platform to provide traceable, explainable medical triage for patients in the EU and US. It delivers asynchronous symptom evaluation and audit logging while strictly enforcing regional data residency and compliance.]

## Key Elements
- Triage API Controller: FastAPI-based component exposing asynchronous endpoints for step-by-step symptom evaluation.
- Inference Engine Component: PyTorch and LangChain-based service running localized diagnostic models to generate urgency scores and plain-language rationales.
- Audit & Traceability Logger: Captures model versions, feature inputs, and output urgency levels for regulatory compliance.
- Feedback Ingestion Component: Handles post-triage patient feedback and escalation metrics.
- Infrastructure: GKE Autopilot with NVIDIA L4 GPU regional node pools in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`.
- Storage & Observability: Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL), Google Artifact Registry, BigQuery via Fluentbit sidecars, and Pub/Sub dead-letter queues.

## Relationships
- Core Backend -> Triage API Controller: Sends symptom evaluation requests and post-triage feedback via gRPC.
- Triage API Controller -> Inference Engine Component: Invokes diagnostic models internally.
- Inference Engine -> Audit & Traceability Logger: Transmits structured reasoning and model version metadata.
- Audit & Traceability Logger -> BigQuery / Cloud SQL: Persists regional audit trails and feedback telemetry.
- Audit & Traceability Logger -> Pub/Sub: Routes failed audit payloads to a dead-letter queue.

## Technology Stack
- Python / FastAPI: Powers the AI Symptom Checker container for high-performance asynchronous API handling.
- PyTorch & LangChain: Executes localized LLM and diagnostic workloads.
- Protobuf / gRPC: Enforces strict data contracts and communication between the Core Backend and FastAPI service.
- GKE Autopilot & NVIDIA L4 GPUs: Provides scalable, managed infrastructure for AI inference workloads.
- OpenTelemetry & Prometheus: Handles distributed tracing and regional performance monitoring.
- BigQuery & Cloud SQL: Ensures partitioned, region-locked storage for HIPAA and GDPR compliance.

## Rationale
[This architecture satisfies EU MDR and HIPAA requirements by enforcing strict regional data residency in GCP and maintaining immutable audit trails for every AI recommendation. Integration / Interoperability Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform delivers secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and AI symptom checking to patients across the EU and US. The architecture enforces strict regional data isolation to maintain GDPR and HIPAA compliance while bridging disparate national healthcare systems.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) and Licensed Clinicians (Primary Users)
- Web Frontend (PWA built with Next.js / React)
- API Gateway (Envoy and Cloud Load Balancing)
- Core Backend Services (Go / Spring Boot)
- AI Symptom Checker (Python / FastAPI)
- Integration / Interoperability Service (Java / Spring Boot / Apache Camel)
- Media Relaying Service (LiveKit SFU/MCU)
- Data Storage (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL and Cloud Storage)
- Regional Messaging & Buffering (Cloud Pub/Sub with Dead Letter Queue)
- External Pharmacies (US & EU National Adapters via eHDSI/NCPeH)

## Relationships
- Web Frontend -> API Gateway: Client requests [HTTPS / WSS]
- API Gateway -> Core Backend Services: API routing [gRPC]
- Core Backend Services -> Integration / Interoperability Service: Triggers prescription workflows [gRPC]
- Integration / Interoperability Service -> External Pharmacies: Sends e-prescriptions [HL7 FHIR / HTTPS / NCPeH]
- Integration / Interoperability Service -> Cloud Pub/Sub: Publishes delivery audit events [PubSub API / gRPC]
- Media Relaying Service -> Patients & Clinicians: Handles real-time video streaming [WebRTC]

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Target cloud provider utilizing `europe-west3` and `us-central1` for data residency.
- Java (Spring Boot / Apache Camel): Core runtime and routing engine for enterprise healthcare interoperability.
- Cloud Pub/Sub: Asynchronous event messaging and Dead Letter Queue management.
- Redis (Memorystore): Distributed cache ensuring idempotency and deduplication.
- OpenTelemetry: Distributed tracing and observability across microservices.

## Rationale
Regional deployment isolation guarantees that EU health data remains in `europe-west3` and US data in `us-central1`, satisfying GDPR and HIPAA constraints. Apache Camel and HL7 FHIR/national adapters ensure seamless interoperability with diverse regional pharmacy networks.

Media Relaying Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. The system ensures regional data residency, strict regulatory compliance (GDPR/HIPAA), and resilient media streaming for unstable rural network connections.

## Key Elements
- Web Frontend (PWA): Next.js/React application for patients and clinicians.
- Media Relaying Service: LiveKit-based SFU/MCU container providing video consultations.
- SFU Media Router: Go-based LiveKit server node handling real-time WebRTC media forwarding and adaptive bitrate scaling.
- Room & Session Manager: Node.js/Go component managing virtual rooms, authentication, and region-locked policies.
- Telemetry & Audit Collector: Go-based component capturing WebRTC stats and compliance metadata.
- TURN/STUN Relay Gateway: Coturn/LiveKit Egress handling NAT traversal and TCP fallback.
- Target Cloud: Google Cloud Platform (GCP) across `europe-west3` and `us-central1` regions.

## Relationships
- Web Frontend (PWA) -> Room & Session Manager: Authenticates and requests connection tokens [gRPC / HTTPS]
- Web Frontend (PWA) <-> SFU Media Router: Relays encrypted audio/video streams [WebRTC over UDP/TCP]
- Web Frontend (PWA) <-> TURN/STUN Relay Gateway: Relays encrypted media via TCP fallback [WebRTC over TLS/TCP]
- SFU Media Router -> Telemetry & Audit Collector: Streams session quality metrics [Internal gRPC]
- Telemetry & Audit Collector -> Core Backend services: Exports aggregated session logs [gRPC]

## Technology Stack
- LiveKit (SFU/MCU): Selected for real-time video and adaptive bitrate streaming to support low-bandwidth resilience.
- Go & Node.js: Used for backend components and media router services to ensure high concurrency and performance.
- GCP Managed Instance Groups (MIGs) / GKE: Deployed in isolated regional clusters to enforce strict data residency.
- Coturn: Implemented for TURN/STUN NAT traversal and TCP/443 fallback in restricted rural networks.

## Rationale
This architecture uses regional GCP deployments to strictly enforce EU and US health data residency constraints. LiveKit and Coturn integrations guarantee stable video consultations for patients in rural areas with unstable internet connections.

Data Storage.analysis:
## Overview
A secure, cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. It enforces strict regional data residency, regulatory compliance, and offline-resilient synchronization.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) and Licensed Clinicians
- Compliance Officers / Auditors
- Web Frontend (PWA) with local SQLite caching
- Core Backend Services (Go / Spring Boot)
- AI Symptom Checker (Python / FastAPI)
- Data Storage: Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL), Google Cloud Storage (WORM buckets)
- Telemetry & Audit: Cloud Logging, BigQuery, Change Data Capture (Debezium / Cloud Pub/Sub)
- Cloud Infrastructure: GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`) with Cloud KMS encryption

## Relationships
- Web Frontend -> Core Backend Services: Synchronizes state and handles mutations [HTTPS / GraphQL]
- Core Backend Services -> Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL): Reads and writes transactional FHIR health records [PostgreSQL Protocol / TLS 1.3]
- Core Backend Services -> Google Cloud Storage: Stores unstructured media and AI traceability inputs [HTTPS / GCP API]
- Core Backend Services -> Change Data Capture: Streams anonymized events [Pub/Sub Protocol]
- Compliance Officers -> BigQuery: Queries immutable audit logs and AI traceability data [SQL / IAM]

## Technology Stack
- **Cloud Provider**: GCP (`europe-west3` for EU, `us-central1` for US) to enforce strict geographical data segregation.
- **Relational Storage**: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL with Row-Level Security for transactional FHIR records and consent states.
- **Object Storage**: Google Cloud Storage region-locked buckets with WORM policies for immutable AI traceability logs and media.
- **Audit & Analytics**: Cloud Logging and BigQuery for scalable, compliant audit querying without database write amplification.
- **Client State**: PWA with SQLite and CRDTs for offline-resilient sync in low-bandwidth rural areas.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict GDPR and HIPAA compliance by logically and physically isolating regional health data while providing immutable audit trails for AI medical device traceability. Furthermore, offline-capable PWA caching guarantees high availability and continuity of care for patients with unstable internet connections.
